title: High-gain vortex transfer via activated forbidden transitions in molecular magnets
authors: Fan Meng, Hao Zhu, Xin-Yao Huang, Guo-Feng Zhang
abstract: Vortex light has garnered considerable interest in recent years owing to its distinctive properties and broad application potential. In this paper, we employ a conventional three-level ladder-type configuration in molecular magnets to realize high-gain vortex light transfer by enabling otherwise forbidden transitions. We demonstrate that the intensity and phase of the generated vortex signal field are governed by the detuning of the probe field and the strength of the control field, and that the topological charges of the incident and generated fields obey a well-defined algebraic relation during the vortex transfer process. Furthermore, we show that, in molecular magnets, the Autler-Townes splitting (ATS) effect yields a larger vortex signal field gain than electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) over a broad parameter range in nonlinear three-wave mixing. This result suggests that the widely accepted view of EIT as the dominant enhancer of nonlinear optical effects may not hold universally. In addition, we revisit previous studies and re-examine the characterization of vortex beam transfer efficiency, emphasizing the need for a more careful interpretation in multi-beam interaction systems. Leveraging the long spin coherence and microwave transitions of molecular magnets, our results may enable quantum information transfer, storage, computing, and radar imaging in solid-state platforms.
summary: This work demonstrates high-gain vortex light transfer in molecular magnets by exploiting symmetry-breaking mechanisms to activate forbidden optical transitions. The theoretical analysis shows that the Autler-Townes splitting effect surpasses EIT in enhancing the signal gain, challenging the universal dominance of EIT in nonlinear optics. The results suggest potential applications for quantum information processing in solid-state quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to achieve high-gain vortex light transfer in molecular magnets by enabling optical transitions that are otherwise forbidden by selection rules.
main_result: The Autler-Townes splitting (ATS) effect was shown to yield a significantly larger signal field gain than Electromagnetically Induced Transparency (EIT) in this specific nonlinear three-wave mixing process.
method: The study employs a theoretical analysis using a three-level ladder-type configuration and solving the Maxwell-Bloch equations under perturbative approximations.
model_or_system: The physical system is the molecular magnet $[	ext{Cr}(	ext{C}_3	ext{S}_5)_3]^{3-}$, modeled by a spin Hamiltonian. The dynamics are analyzed using a three-level ladder configuration, where symmetry breaking allows nominally forbidden transitions.
key_observables: Intensity and phase of the generated vortex signal field; the topological charges of the incident and generated fields.
important_parameters: Detuning of the probe field, strength of the control field, and the ratio of signal gain between ATS and EIT.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the absence of nuclear spins to suppress decoherence and relies on the perturbative approximation for weak probe and signal fields.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the three-level ladder configuration with broken symmetry, showing the nonlinear three-wave mixing process generating a signal field.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model using a three-level ladder system, derives the coupled equations for field propagation, calculates the field amplitudes using steady-state solutions, and compares the gain mechanisms (ATS vs. EIT).
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, solid-state platform (molecular magnets) to study fundamental quantum optics phenomena like forbidden transition enhancement, offering a novel comparison between EIT and ATS in a highly controllable solid-state environment.
